recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current build-scope source already conveys the FHIR-13752 rule, as refined by later published search guidance; another wording edit would duplicate or risk destabilizing the existing guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-13752 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core issue asking that the Search page's "Specifying the type of Resource"/_type language be fixed to match REST Variant Searches. The concern was that the Search page could be read as allowing only parameters that apply to all resources even when _type named multiple resource types, while the REST page allowed parameters common to the named types.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 12719. Converted git commit 13705e55a3fd555a4167d7814f373e0f588e26fe (#13752 - clarify about search all parameters) changed source/http.html in the Variant Searches area. Later commit c6fb216ed04cdc382687bf2cd72c5f0861ff76f5 changed source/search.html so the no-type case is limited to all-resource base parameters while the multiple-type case can use search parameters shared across the specified resources.
additional_context: The original implementers Zulip thread confirms the intended distinction: Grahame Grieve explained that the quoted all-resource-only sentence predated parameters common across multiple types. Later Published issue FHIR-36347 revisited the same HTTP/Search consistency area for R5; its audit commit is already on the combined branch and confirms that current source/http.html delegates parameter availability to source/search.html while source/search.html states separate no-type, single-type, and multiple-type rules. FHIR-23557, a later typo correction for the same sentence, is also already represented on the combined branch. No Confluence reference to FHIR-13752 was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html already says that no _type permits only all-resource base parameters, one _type permits that type's parameters, and multiple _type values permit parameters commonly referenced between resources. Current source/http.html points to search.html#type for parameter availability instead of maintaining conflicting local rules.
